newsitem.title: USA: Japan, US statement deliberately vague - official.
newsitem.headline: Japan, US statement deliberately vague - official.

text.p: Japan and the United States made a deliberately vague statement on currency after a bilateral meeting on Sunday, to avoid unnecessary market reaction, a senior Japanese Finance Ministry official said.
Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka and Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said in their statement that they were concerned by recent developments of the Japanese yen.
The ministry official, who briefed reporters on the meeting, said Japan and the United States had agreed not to specifically say what they meant by "concern about recent develoments of the yen."

The statement also said Mitsuzuka and Rubin reaffirmed their commitment to cooperate closely in foreign exchange markets as appropriate. But the statement did not specifically say what kind of currency situation would require cooperative action.
"We did not mention those points questioned because any specific references may cause unnecessary market reaction," the official said.
The official said Mitsuzuka spent a lot of time at the 50-minute meeting with Rubin in explaining that Japan's surplus in goods and services trade is unlikely to rise significantly in the future.

Mitsuzuka and Rubin held a bilateral meeting ahead of a meeting later Sunday of the finance ministers and central bank chiefs from the Group of Seven industrialized nations -- Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, and the United States.
